title: Residential Electricity Supply Cancellation, Drop and Withdrawal Rules
content:
Care desk rule, Residential Electricity Supply. The customer cancels an active agreement by confirming the cancellation; Beacon Ridge then schedules a drop that takes effect on the premise's next scheduled meter read date, which is recorded on the agreement as the drop effective date. The date the customer confirmed is recorded as the drop requested date, and the agreement becomes drop pending.

## Withdrawing a cancellation

The customer may withdraw the cancellation and keep the agreement on its existing terms. A withdrawal is accepted only when the customer withdraws the cancellation before the scheduled drop takes effect on the drop effective date. Day one is the calendar day after the drop requested date, and the withdrawal period closes at the end of the calendar day before the drop effective date; the cut-off is 0 calendar days ahead of the drop effective date, so the drop effective date itself falls outside the period. The test is made against the drop effective date recorded on the agreement. A withdrawal returns the agreement to active and clears the recorded drop dates and drop reason.

| Drop requested (hypothetical) | Drop effective date | Withdrawal asked | Accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| June 3 | June 18 | June 17 | yes, last day of the period |
| June 3 | June 18 | June 18 | no, the drop takes effect that day |
| June 3 | June 18 | June 4 | yes, day one |

## How supply ends

- When the utility completes the drop, the agreement closes with the close reason "cancelled by customer", or "move out" when the drop reason was a move-out.
- When the utility ends supply because another supplier enrolled the premise, the agreement closes with the close reason "switched to other supplier".
- When the utility final-bills the premise for a move-out without a Beacon Ridge cancellation, it closes with the close reason "move out".

A cancellation or switch-away does not cancel bill credits already posted.
